note.explanation: A network topology describes how devices (nodes) are arranged and connected. The main types in this section are bus, star, ring, and mesh.
examples: In a star topology, a central switch or hub connects to the other devices.
In a mesh topology, every device connects to every other device.
note.simple: Topology is the shape or pattern of the connections between devices in a network.
note.checkQuestion: Which topology connects each device to every other device?

written.text: Compare and contrast the different types of network topologies (star, ring, bus, and mesh).
written.finalAnswer: Bus topology uses one shared communication line; if its main cable fails, the whole network goes down. Star topology connects each node through a central switch or hub, which works as a data flow repeater. Ring topology connects devices in a circular pathway and data travels in one direction; one failed connection can affect the whole network, although a 2-way ring can help to some extent. Mesh topology connects each device to every other device, providing high redundancy and reliability because data can use alternative routes.

explain.title: What topology means
explain.body: Network topologies are methods used to define the arrangement of different devices in a computer network, where each device is called a node. The reliability and performance of a network are impacted by the way its devices are linked.

explain.title: Bus topology
explain.body: In a Bus topology, all devices share a single communication line called a bus. Each device is connected to this central cable. If the main cable fails, the whole network goes down.

explain.title: Star and ring topologies
explain.body: In a star topology each node in network communicates with the others via a central switch or hub. The hub works as a data flow repeater. In a Ring topology, each device is connected in a circular pathway with other devices. Data travels in one direction, passing through each device.

explain.title: Mesh topology
explain.body: In a Mesh topology, each device is connected to every other device. This provides high redundancy and reliability. If one link fails, data can be rerouted through other links.

mistakes: Do not confuse a bus, which has one shared communication line, with a star, which uses a central switch or hub.
Do not say that ring data travels in every direction; this section says it travels in one direction.
Do not describe mesh as having only one connection path; its multiple links provide alternative routes.
When comparing topologies, do not give only their names—include how the devices are connected and an important feature or weakness.
